The regression was in `sqlparse/tokens.py`'s `_TokenType.__getattr__`. It had a comment "don't mess with dunder" but no actual code enforcing that — so any dunder attribute lookup (e.g. `__deepcopy__`, `__reduce_ex__`, `__copy__`) used by the `copy` module would create and return a new `_TokenType` instance instead of raising `AttributeError`. When `copy.deepcopy()`/`copy.copy()` then tried to call these looked-up attributes as methods, it hit `TypeError: '_TokenType' object is not callable'`.

Fix: added the actual guard so dunder-named attribute lookups raise `AttributeError` (letting Python fall back to default behavior) instead of synthesizing a new token type:

```python
def __getattr__(self, name):
    # don't mess with dunder
    if name.startswith('__') and name.endswith('__'):
        raise AttributeError
    new = _TokenType(self + (name,))
    setattr(self, name, new)
    new.parent = self
    return new
```

Verified with `copy.deepcopy()` on a parsed statement, which now works correctly and returns `SELECT 1` instead of raising the TypeError. This checkout has no local `tests/` directory (only the `sqlparse` package and docs/benchmarks), so the hidden upstream tests will be run externally against this fix.
